title_ar: من محمد الحسن بن الدَّدَوْ إلى كل من يصل إليه من المسلمين
title_en: From Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew to Every Muslim Whom This Reaches
body_ar:
السلام عليكم و رحمة الله و بركاته
أمَّا بعدُ فإِن من أفضل مواسم الخير في السنة هذا الموسم الذي امْتَنَّ الله به عليكم في هذه الأيام الفاضلة التي هي أفضل أيَّام السنة، فقد أخرج الجماعة إلا مسلماً و النسائي من حديث ابن عباسٍ رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «ما من أيَّامٍ العمل الصالح فيها أحب إلى الله عزَّ وجلَّ من هذه الأيَّام. يعنى عشر ذي الحجَّة» وأخرج أحمد و غيره من حديث ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من أيَّامٍ أعظمُ عند الله سبحانه ولا أحب إليه العمل فيهِنَّ من هذه الأيَّام العشر، فأكثروا فيهن من التهليل والتكبير والتحميد.» فاجتهدوا في الأعمال الصالحة في هذه الأيام خصوصا الأعمال التالية:

1 - صومها جميعا: فقد أخرج أحمد والنسائي عن حفصة بنت عمر رضي الله عنهما قالت: «أربع لم يكن يدعهن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صيام عاشوراء والعشر وثلاثة أيام من كل شهر والركعتين قبل الغداة.» والمقصود ما عدا يوم العيد فلا يحل صومه، ولذلك أخرج أبو داوو د عن بعض أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصوم تسع ذي الحجة ويوم عاشوراء وثلاثة أيام من كل شهر وأول اثنين من الشهر والخميسَ.» وأمَّا حديث عائشة عند مسلم: «ما رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صائما في العشر قط .» فمحمُول على الحج.
2 - صوم يوم عرفة بخصوصه لغير الحاج: فقد أخرج مسلم وأحمد وأبو داوو د وابن ماجه عن أبي قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «صوم يوم عرفة يُكفِّرُ سنتين ماضية و مستقبلة و صوم يوم عاشوراءَ يكفر سنةً ماضية.» وفي لفظ: «أحتسب على الله أن يكفر السنة التي قبله و السنة التي بعده.»
3 - الإكثار من الذكر: فقد قال البخاري في الصحيح: «وقال ابن عباس: ﴿ويذكروا اسم الله في أيام معلومات﴾ أيام العشر. قال: وكان ابن عمر وأبو هريرة يخرجان إلى السوق في أيام العشر يكبرانِ ويكبِّر الناس بتكبيرهما.» وقد سبق في حديث ابن عمر الإكثار من التهليل والتكبير والتحميد.
4 - عدم أخذ المضحي من شعره وأظافره من بداية الشهر حتى يضحي تشبها بالمحرم: فقد أخرج الجماعة إلا البخاري من حديث أم سلمة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من كان له ذِبحٌ يذبحه فإِذا أهلَّ هلال ذي الحجة فلا يأخذن من شعره وأظافره حتى يضحي.»
والله يوفقنا وإياكم لكل خير ويتقبل منا ومنكم.
كتبه محمد الحسن بن الددو كان الله له وليّاً ونصيراً
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.
To proceed: among the best seasons of good in the year is this season with which God has favoured you in these days of merit, which are the best days of the year. The Group narrated — except Muslim and al-Nasa'i — from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said: «There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to God, mighty and majestic, than these days» — meaning the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. And Ahmad and others narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said: «There are no days greater in the sight of God, glorified is He, nor in which deeds are more beloved to Him, than these ten days; so do much in them of declaring God's oneness, of declaring His greatness and of praising Him.» So exert yourselves in righteous deeds in these days, and especially in the following:

1 - Fasting all of them. Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated from Hafsa bint Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: «Four things the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, did not leave: the fast of Ashura, the ten days, three days of every month, and the two cycles before the morning meal.» What is meant is all but the day of Eid, for fasting it is not lawful. For this reason Abu Dawud narrated from one of the wives of the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, who said: «The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast the nine days of Dhu al-Hijjah, the day of Ashura, three days of every month, and the first Monday of the month, and the Thursdays.» As for the hadith of Aisha with Muslim: «I never saw the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, fasting in the ten days at all.» — that is to be understood as referring to the Hajj.
2 - Fasting the day of Arafah in particular, for one who is not on Hajj. Muslim, Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from Abu Qatada, may God be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Fasting the day of Arafah expiates two years, one past and one to come; and fasting the day of Ashura expiates one past year.» And in another wording: «I reckon upon God that He will expiate the year before it and the year after it.»
3 - Doing much remembrance of God. Al-Bukhari said in the Ṣaḥīḥ: «And Ibn Abbas said: {and that they may mention the name of God on the appointed days} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:28) — the days of the ten. He said: and Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayra used to go out to the market during the days of the ten, declaring God's greatness, and the people would declare His greatness at their declaring it.» And there has already come, in the hadith of Ibn Umar, the instruction to do much of declaring God's oneness, declaring His greatness and praising Him.
4 - That one who is going to offer the Eid sacrifice (uḍḥiyah) not take anything from his hair or his nails from the beginning of the month until he has sacrificed, in resemblance to one in the consecrated state of pilgrimage (muḥrim). The Group narrated — except al-Bukhari — from the hadith of Umm Salama, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Whoever has an animal to slaughter that he is going to slaughter — when the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah appears, let him not take anything from his hair or his nails until he has sacrificed.»
And God grant us and you every good, and accept from us and from you.
Written by Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew, may God be for him a protector and a helper

flags.arabic: أخرج الجماعة إلا مسلما و النسائي
flags.context: the attribution of the first hadith, and again of the last with al-Bukhari excepted
options: The Group narrated — except Muslim and al-Nasa'i
It was narrated by all the principal collectors except Muslim and al-Nasa'i
The six narrated it apart from Muslim and al-Nasa'i
flags.note: al-jamāʿah is a fixed term of hadith citation for the set of principal collectors — conventionally Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, though the membership differs between authors. It is not in the glossary. 'The Group' is the established English rendering and has been kept, because naming the collectors would assert a membership the Sheikh has not specified. Option 2 loses the term of art; option 3 asserts a count.

flags.context: the name of the collector, twice in the record
options: preserve the source spelling in body_ar and render 'Abu Dawud' in body_en
reproduce the broken spelling in the English too
flags.note: The source spells أبو داود as أبو داوو د, with a doubled wāw and a space before the final dāl, in both places it occurs. This is a CMS or typing defect, not a variant name. Style guide section 11 forbids silently fixing the source, so body_ar carries it as served and the English gives the name correctly. Flagged so the defect is visible.

flags.context: the fourth item in the hadith of Hafsa
options: and the two cycles before the morning meal
and the two cycles before the dawn prayer
and the two rakʿahs before breakfast
flags.note: al-ghadāh in this hadith is read by some as the morning meal and by others as the dawn (ṣubḥ) prayer, and the received text in several collections has الغداة meaning the dawn prayer, i.e. the two sunnah cycles before fajr. The two readings give different acts. The Sheikh does not comment on it, so the question is left open here rather than settled.

flags.context: the Sheikh's reconciliation of Aisha's hadith with the others
options: that is to be understood as referring to the Hajj
it is to be carried on the case of the pilgrimage
it applies only to when he was performing Hajj
flags.note: maḥmūl ʿalā is a technical move in uṣūl: a report is 'carried upon' a particular case so that it does not conflict with another. Option 2 is the literal calque and is opaque in English; option 3 states the result but drops the reasoning, which style guide section 1 requires be preserved. Option 0 keeps both.

flags.context: the hadith of Umm Salama on not cutting hair or nails
options: Whoever has an animal to slaughter that he is going to slaughter
Whoever has a sacrificial animal to offer
Whoever intends to make a sacrifice
flags.note: dhibḥ is the animal itself, not the act and not the intention. Option 2 reads the ruling onto intention, which is a live question among the jurists and one the Sheikh does not address here.

flags.arabic: من محمد الحسن بن الدَّدَوْ إلى كل من يصل إليه من المسلمين
flags.context: records 1328 and 1381 carry the identical text under two IDs
options: treat 1381 as a re-publication of 1328 for a later year and display one, noting both dates
keep both as served pending the Sheikh's office
flags.note: Duplicate body, style guide section 11. Record 1328 (published 30 June 2022) and record 1381 (published 11 June 2024) have identical titles and, once whitespace is normalised, character-for-character identical bodies of 2,088 characters. They differ only in that six blank-line separators in 1328 are single line breaks in 1381 (2,095 against 2,089 characters). Both fall just before Dhu al-Hijjah in their respective years, so this looks like the same seasonal letter re-issued rather than a CMS accident of the kind recorded at 396/397/400. Flagged, not deduplicated: the decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

translator_notes: This is a written address from the Sheikh to the Muslims at large, signed at the foot in his own name, not a news report and not a fatwa in answer to a question. It is typed 'article' although the CMS files it under the news section; there is precedent for this in the corpus.
Hadith attributions are preserved exactly as the Sheikh gives them, with no grading added and none dropped. Where he names only the collectors, only the collectors appear in the English.

The Qur'anic fragment is rendered in curly quotation marks with a reference per style guide section 4, inside the quotation from al-Bukhari where the Sheikh places it. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and not a substitute for the Arabic. The source encloses it in ornate Qur'anic brackets, which body_ar preserves.
The French-style guillemets around the hadith texts are the source's own and are kept in both languages so the quoted material stays visibly bounded.

التهليل، التكبير، التحميد are rendered by what they mean — declaring God's oneness, declaring His greatness, praising Him — rather than left as transliterations, per the house rule that an untranslated Arabic term is not a translation. These are recited formulae, so if the site ever sets them out individually the Arabic must accompany them (style guide section 4).
الأضحية is bracketed on first occurrence using the glossary's 'the Eid sacrifice'; المحرم is glossed from the glossary's iḥrām entry.

The four acts are given as recommendations and encouragements, and no ruling word (wājib, mustaḥabb, makrūh) appears in the Arabic. None has been supplied. The one negative ruling stated is that fasting the day of Eid is not lawful, and that is rendered as the Arabic has it.

This record is the later of the two publications of this letter; see the duplicate flag and record 1328. The body is identical to 1328's apart from six paragraph separators, which are single line breaks here and blank lines there. The paragraph structure of body_en follows this record's own Arabic, not 1328's.
The title's الدَّدَوْ carries full vowelling, which body_ar preserves; the name is given in body_en in the corpus's standard unvowelled romanisation, al-Dedew.
